**Ashland** is a city in [Ashland County, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland_County,_Ohio "Ashland County, Ohio"), United States, and its [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-GR6-6) It is approximately 66 miles (106 km) southwest of [Cleveland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland "Cleveland"). The population was 19,225 at the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"). It is the center of the Ashland [Micropolitan statistical area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micropolitan_statistical_area "Micropolitan statistical area"), which includes all of Ashland County.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Ashland was laid out by William Montgomery[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-8) in 1815. Ashland was originally called Uniontown, but in 1822 the city was compelled to adopt a new name because another city in Ohio was already named [Uniontown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniontown,_Ohio "Uniontown, Ohio"). The new name of Ashland was selected by supporters of the Kentucky congressman [Henry Clay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay "Henry Clay"), from [Ashland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland_(Henry_Clay_estate) "Ashland (Henry Clay estate)"), his estate near Lexington.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-10) Later, "Henry Clay High School" was considered as a name for what is now known as [Ashland High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland_High_School_(Ohio) "Ashland High School (Ohio)").

In the mid-1800s, Ashland pioneers traveled to [Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon "Oregon"), naming a [settlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Oregon "Ashland, Oregon") after the town. In 1878, with financial assistance from the city, the German Baptist [Brethren Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brethren_Church "Brethren Church") opened [Ashland College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland_College "Ashland College").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-11) Ashland became an early center of manufacturing in Ohio. In 1870, brothers Francis E. Myers and Philip A. Myers went into business selling farm equipment and operating a repair shop. They secured the patent for a double-action pump that delivered water in a steady stream rather than spurts. By 1915, F.E. Myers & Bro. had 800 workers. Myers was the largest of the 47 factories in Ashland at that time.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-Shellhouse-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-13) Other factories included Reliable Match Co. ("Strike Anywhere Matches"), Kauffman Mfg. Co. (manufacturer of folding chairs used in Union Army encampments), Dr. Hess & Clark (veterinary supplies and disinfectants) and T.W. Miller's Faultless Rubber Co. (rubber sundries, surgical goods and bicycle tires).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-Shellhouse-12)

In 1912, Harry Ross Gill, an Ashland native, invented the way to make cigar-shaped balloons (until then they were only round).[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-14) He started the Eagle Rubber Company in 1913 and the National Latex company in 1929.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-History-15) The industry that Gill developed in Ashland led to the city becoming known as "the balloon capital of the world."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-History-15) Ashland still celebrates its balloon heritage with its annual BalloonFest.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-16)

Ashland was designated a [Tree City USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree_City_USA "Tree City USA") by the [National Arbor Day Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arbor_Day "Arbor Day") in 1984.

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geography")]

According to the 2010 census, the city has an area of 11.23 square miles (29.1 km 2), of which 11.17 square miles (28.9 km 2) (or 99.47%) is land and 0.06 square miles (0.16 km 2) (or 0.53%) is water.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-17)

The city has 85.6 miles (137.8 km) of streets, one hospital, two fire stations,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-18) one police station, and five parks.

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Ashland had a population of 19,225. The median age was 40.5 years. 19.7% of residents were under the age of 18 and 22.3% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 88.1 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 84.0 males age 18 and over.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-Census2020DP-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-Census2020PL-21)

99.5% of residents lived in urban areas, while 0.5% lived in rural areas.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-Census2020DHC-22)

There were 8,140 households in Ashland, of which 23.9% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 39.1% were married-couple households, 19.4% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 33.6% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 37.5% of all households were made up of individuals and 17.2% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-Census2020DP-20)

There were 8,939 housing units, of which 8.9% were vacant. Among occupied housing units, 60.1% were owner-occupied and 39.9% were renter-occupied. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.3% and the rental vacancy rate was 6.5%.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-Census2020DP-20)

### 2010 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2010 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-wwwcensusgov-23) of 2010, the city had 20,362 people, 8,063 households, and 4,813 families. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 1,822.9 inhabitants per square mile (703.8/km 2). There were 8,914 housing units at an average density of 798.0 units per square mile (308.1 units/km 2). The city's racial makeup was 95.8% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 1.4% [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census) "African American (U.S. Census)"), 0.1% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 1.0% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.1% [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(U.S._Census) "Race (U.S. Census)"), 0.3% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(U.S._Census) "Race (U.S. Census)"), and 1.3% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") of any race were 1.2% of the population.

There were 8,063 households, of which 28.2% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 43.2% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 12.1% had a female householder with no husband present, 4.4% had a male householder with no wife present, and 40.3% were non-families. 34.2% of all households were made up of individuals, and 15.9% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.28 and the average family size was 2.91.

The city's median age was 36.1 years. 21% of the city's population was under age 18; 15.7% was from age 18 to 24; 22.5% was from age 25 to 44; 23.1% was from age 45 to 64; and 17.7% was age 65 or older. The city's gender makeup was 46.8% male and 53.2% female.

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

As of the census[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-GR2-5) of 2000, the city had 21,249 people, 8,327 households, and 5,262 families. The population density was 2,051.5 inhabitants per square mile (792.1/km 2). There were 8,870 housing units at an average density of 856.4 units per square mile (330.7 units/km 2). The city's racial makeup was 96.35% White, 1.19% African American, 0.13% Native American, 1.05% Asian, 0.05% [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islander_(U.S._Census) "Pacific Islander (U.S. Census)"), 0.32% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), and 0.91% from two or more races. Hispanic or Latino of any race were 0.85% of the population.

There were 8,327 households, of which 29.1% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 48.3% were married couples living together, 11.4% had a female householder with no husband present, and 36.8% were non-families. 31.8% of all households were made up of individuals, and 13.8% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.32 and the average family size was 2.92.

22.6% of the city's population was under age 18, 15.4% was from age 18 to 24, 25.1% was from age 25 to 44, 20.3% was from age 45 to 64, and 16.6% was age 65 or older. The median age was 35 years. For every 100 females, there were 87.2 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 82.0 males.

The city's median household income was $34,250, and the median family income was $42,755. Males had a median income of $33,634 versus $21,781 for females. The city's [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") was $16,760. About 7.9% of families and 10.5% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 13.7% of those under age 18 and 9.1% of those age 65 or over.

## Parks and attractions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Parks and attractions")]

The City of Ashland Parks and Recreation Department is responsible for maintaining 360 acres of parks, playgrounds, hiking trails, and other public facilities.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-24)

## Government

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Government")]

The city is governed by a [mayor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor "Mayor"), Matt Miller, and a five-person [city council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_council "City council").

As of 2026, the mayor's salary is $106,559.00.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-25)

### Police

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Police")]

The Ashland City Chief of Police is David Lay. The Ashland County sheriff is Kurt J. Schneider. The Chief Deputy is David Blake. The Ashland County Jail holds on average 110 inmates a day and 1750 per year.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-26)

### Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Transportation")]

The [Ashland County Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland_County_Airport "Ashland County Airport") is three nautical miles (3.5 mi; 5.6 km) northeast of Ashland's [central business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-27)

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Education")]

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/Ashland_Public_Library.JPG/250px-Ashland_Public_Library.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ashland_Public_Library.JPG)

Ashland Public Library

The [Ashland City School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland_City_School_District "Ashland City School District") enrolls 3,192 students in public [primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_education "Primary education") and [secondary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_education "Secondary education") schools as of the 2017–18 school year.[3904350](https://nces.ed.gov/ccd/districtsearch/district_detail.asp?Search=2&ID2=3904350)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-nces_dist-28) The district operates five schools, including three elementary schools, one middle school, one high school. The Ashland City School District superintendent is Steve Paramore. The city is also home to Ashland Christian School, St. Edward Catholic School, and Ashland Montessori School.

The city is home to [Ashland University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland_University "Ashland University") and [Ashland Theological Seminary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland_Theological_Seminary "Ashland Theological Seminary"). Both were established by [the Brethren Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brethren_Church "The Brethren Church")—an [Evangelical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evangelical "Evangelical")[Protestant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestant "Protestant") church in the [Anabaptist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anabaptist "Anabaptist") tradition—which is headquartered in Ashland.

Ashland contains the Ashland Public Library.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-29) The library provides free access to computers and wifi, reservable meeting rooms, materials, [Golden Buckeye Card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Buckeye_Card?action=edit&redlink=1 "Golden Buckeye Card (page does not exist)") applications, tech coaching, voter registration, and library events. All programs held at the library are entirely free for patrons. The APL has three library vehicles; two act as bookmobiles for the community. Obtaining a library card is free and the library is now a fine free establishment.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-30)

**Ashland** is a city in [Ashland County, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland_County,_Ohio "Ashland County, Ohio"), United States, and its [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-GR6-6) It is approximately 66 miles (106 km) southwest of [Cleveland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland "Cleveland"). The population was 19,225 at the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"). It is the center of the Ashland [Micropolitan statistical area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micropolitan_statistical_area "Micropolitan statistical area"), which includes all of Ashland County.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Ashland was laid out by William Montgomery[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-8) in 1815. Ashland was originally called Uniontown, but in 1822 the city was compelled to adopt a new name because another city in Ohio was already named [Uniontown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniontown,_Ohio "Uniontown, Ohio"). The new name of Ashland was selected by supporters of the Kentucky congressman [Henry Clay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay "Henry Clay"), from [Ashland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland_(Henry_Clay_estate) "Ashland (Henry Clay estate)"), his estate near Lexington.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-10) Later, "Henry Clay High School" was considered as a name for what is now known as [Ashland High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland_High_School_(Ohio) "Ashland High School (Ohio)").

In the mid-1800s, Ashland pioneers traveled to [Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon "Oregon"), naming a [settlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Oregon "Ashland, Oregon") after the town. In 1878, with financial assistance from the city, the German Baptist [Brethren Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brethren_Church "Brethren Church") opened [Ashland College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland_College "Ashland College").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-11) Ashland became an early center of manufacturing in Ohio. In 1870, brothers Francis E. Myers and Philip A. Myers went into business selling farm equipment and operating a repair shop. They secured the patent for a double-action pump that delivered water in a steady stream rather than spurts. By 1915, F.E. Myers & Bro. had 800 workers. Myers was the largest of the 47 factories in Ashland at that time.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-Shellhouse-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-13) Other factories included Reliable Match Co. ("Strike Anywhere Matches"), Kauffman Mfg. Co. (manufacturer of folding chairs used in Union Army encampments), Dr. Hess & Clark (veterinary supplies and disinfectants) and T.W. Miller's Faultless Rubber Co. (rubber sundries, surgical goods and bicycle tires).[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-Shellhouse-12)

In 1912, Harry Ross Gill, an Ashland native, invented the way to make cigar-shaped balloons (until then they were only round).[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-14) He started the Eagle Rubber Company in 1913 and the National Latex company in 1929.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-History-15) The industry that Gill developed in Ashland led to the city becoming known as "the balloon capital of the world."[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-History-15) Ashland still celebrates its balloon heritage with its annual BalloonFest.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-16)

Ashland was designated a [Tree City USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree_City_USA "Tree City USA") by the [National Arbor Day Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arbor_Day "Arbor Day") in 1984.

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geography")]

According to the 2010 census, the city has an area of 11.23 square miles (29.1 km 2), of which 11.17 square miles (28.9 km 2) (or 99.47%) is land and 0.06 square miles (0.16 km 2) (or 0.53%) is water.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-17)

The city has 85.6 miles (137.8 km) of streets, one hospital, two fire stations,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-18) one police station, and five parks.

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Ashland had a population of 19,225. The median age was 40.5 years. 19.7% of residents were under the age of 18 and 22.3% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 88.1 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 84.0 males age 18 and over.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-Census2020DP-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-Census2020PL-21)

99.5% of residents lived in urban areas, while 0.5% lived in rural areas.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-Census2020DHC-22)

There were 8,140 households in Ashland, of which 23.9% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 39.1% were married-couple households, 19.4% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 33.6% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 37.5% of all households were made up of individuals and 17.2% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-Census2020DP-20)

There were 8,939 housing units, of which 8.9% were vacant. Among occupied housing units, 60.1% were owner-occupied and 39.9% were renter-occupied. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.3% and the rental vacancy rate was 6.5%.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-Census2020DP-20)

### 2010 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2010 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-wwwcensusgov-23) of 2010, the city had 20,362 people, 8,063 households, and 4,813 families. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 1,822.9 inhabitants per square mile (703.8/km 2). There were 8,914 housing units at an average density of 798.0 units per square mile (308.1 units/km 2). The city's racial makeup was 95.8% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 1.4% [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census) "African American (U.S. Census)"), 0.1% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 1.0% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.1% [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(U.S._Census) "Race (U.S. Census)"), 0.3% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(U.S._Census) "Race (U.S. Census)"), and 1.3% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") of any race were 1.2% of the population.

There were 8,063 households, of which 28.2% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 43.2% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 12.1% had a female householder with no husband present, 4.4% had a male householder with no wife present, and 40.3% were non-families. 34.2% of all households were made up of individuals, and 15.9% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.28 and the average family size was 2.91.

The city's median age was 36.1 years. 21% of the city's population was under age 18; 15.7% was from age 18 to 24; 22.5% was from age 25 to 44; 23.1% was from age 45 to 64; and 17.7% was age 65 or older. The city's gender makeup was 46.8% male and 53.2% female.

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

As of the census[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-GR2-5) of 2000, the city had 21,249 people, 8,327 households, and 5,262 families. The population density was 2,051.5 inhabitants per square mile (792.1/km 2). There were 8,870 housing units at an average density of 856.4 units per square mile (330.7 units/km 2). The city's racial makeup was 96.35% White, 1.19% African American, 0.13% Native American, 1.05% Asian, 0.05% [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islander_(U.S._Census) "Pacific Islander (U.S. Census)"), 0.32% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), and 0.91% from two or more races. Hispanic or Latino of any race were 0.85% of the population.

There were 8,327 households, of which 29.1% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 48.3% were married couples living together, 11.4% had a female householder with no husband present, and 36.8% were non-families. 31.8% of all households were made up of individuals, and 13.8% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.32 and the average family size was 2.92.

22.6% of the city's population was under age 18, 15.4% was from age 18 to 24, 25.1% was from age 25 to 44, 20.3% was from age 45 to 64, and 16.6% was age 65 or older. The median age was 35 years. For every 100 females, there were 87.2 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 82.0 males.

The city's median household income was $34,250, and the median family income was $42,755. Males had a median income of $33,634 versus $21,781 for females. The city's [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") was $16,760. About 7.9% of families and 10.5% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 13.7% of those under age 18 and 9.1% of those age 65 or over.

## Parks and attractions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Parks and attractions")]

The City of Ashland Parks and Recreation Department is responsible for maintaining 360 acres of parks, playgrounds, hiking trails, and other public facilities.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-24)

## Government

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Government")]

The city is governed by a [mayor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor "Mayor"), Matt Miller, and a five-person [city council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_council "City council").

As of 2026, the mayor's salary is $106,559.00.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-25)

### Police

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Police")]

The Ashland City Chief of Police is David Lay. The Ashland County sheriff is Kurt J. Schneider. The Chief Deputy is David Blake. The Ashland County Jail holds on average 110 inmates a day and 1750 per year.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-26)

### Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Transportation")]

The [Ashland County Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland_County_Airport "Ashland County Airport") is three nautical miles (3.5 mi; 5.6 km) northeast of Ashland's [central business district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_business_district "Central business district").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-27)

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashland,_Ohio&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Education")]

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/Ashland_Public_Library.JPG/250px-Ashland_Public_Library.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ashland_Public_Library.JPG)

Ashland Public Library

The [Ashland City School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland_City_School_District "Ashland City School District") enrolls 3,192 students in public [primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_education "Primary education") and [secondary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_education "Secondary education") schools as of the 2017–18 school year.[3904350](https://nces.ed.gov/ccd/districtsearch/district_detail.asp?Search=2&ID2=3904350)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-nces_dist-28) The district operates five schools, including three elementary schools, one middle school, one high school. The Ashland City School District superintendent is Steve Paramore. The city is also home to Ashland Christian School, St. Edward Catholic School, and Ashland Montessori School.

The city is home to [Ashland University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland_University "Ashland University") and [Ashland Theological Seminary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland_Theological_Seminary "Ashland Theological Seminary"). Both were established by [the Brethren Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brethren_Church "The Brethren Church")—an [Evangelical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evangelical "Evangelical")[Protestant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protestant "Protestant") church in the [Anabaptist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anabaptist "Anabaptist") tradition—which is headquartered in Ashland.

Ashland contains the Ashland Public Library.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-29) The library provides free access to computers and wifi, reservable meeting rooms, materials, [Golden Buckeye Card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Buckeye_Card?action=edit&redlink=1 "Golden Buckeye Card (page does not exist)") applications, tech coaching, voter registration, and library events. All programs held at the library are entirely free for patrons. The APL has three library vehicles; two act as bookmobiles for the community. Obtaining a library card is free and the library is now a fine free establishment.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland,_Ohio#cite_note-30)

**Ashburn** is an [unincorporated settlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unincorporated_area#United_States "Unincorporated area") and [census-designated place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census-designated_place "Census-designated place") (CDP) in [Loudoun County, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_County,_Virginia "Loudoun County, Virginia"), United States. At the [2020 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), its population was 46,349,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-Census_2020-3) up from 3,393 in 1990. It is 30 miles (48 km) northwest of Washington, D.C., and part of the [Washington metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_metropolitan_area "Washington metropolitan area"). Ashburn is a major hub for [Internet traffic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_traffic "Internet traffic") due to its many [data centers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_center "Data center").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-6)

## Etymology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashburn,_Virginia&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Etymology")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8c/2018-10-25_14_33_59_View_west_along_Virginia_State_Route_267_%28Dulles_Greenway%29_at_Exit_5_%28Virginia_State_Route_901-Claiborne_Parkway%2C_Ashburn_Farm%2C_Broadlands%29_in_Broadlands%2C_Loudoun_County%2C_Virginia.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2018-10-25_14_33_59_View_west_along_Virginia_State_Route_267_(Dulles_Greenway)_at_Exit_5_(Virginia_State_Route_901-Claiborne_Parkway,_Ashburn_Farm,_Broadlands)_in_Broadlands,_Loudoun_County,_Virginia.jpg)

Dulles Greenway Exit 5 on to Claiborne Parkway toward Ashburn Farm

The name Ashburn is believed to have originated from "Ashburn Farm," a 1,236-acre estate originally owned by [John Janney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Janney "John Janney"), a prominent 19th-century [Quaker lawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quakers "Quakers") and politician who served as president of Virginia's Secession Convention in 1861. The property was later purchased by George Lee III in the 1870s, who is thought to have named it "Ashburn" either for the [ash trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraxinus "Fraxinus") that dotted the landscape or possibly as a reference to the ash-colored soil or [barn fires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barn_fire "Barn fire") that had previously occurred in the area.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-7) Originally a quiet farming village known as Farmwell, the area became a part of a larger plantation economy in [Loudoun County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_County,_Virginia "Loudoun County, Virginia"). Ashburn remained largely rural through the early 20th century. It began to change significantly in the 1980s and 1990s with the expansion of the [Dulles Technology Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_Technology_Corridor "Dulles Technology Corridor") and the construction of large neighborhoods such as [Ashburn Village](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn_Village "Ashburn Village") and Ashburn Farm.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-8)

Today, Ashburn is a central part of [Loudoun County's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_County,_Virginia "Loudoun County, Virginia") high-tech economy and suburban expansion with preserved natural and historic landscapes such as the [W&OD Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_and_Old_Dominion_Railroad_Regional_Park "Washington and Old Dominion Railroad Regional Park") and nearby farms and battlefields.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-9)

According to the [US Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), Ashburn is a [census designated place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census-designated_place "Census-designated place"). Despite being restricted to a certain boundary, the broader "Ashburn area" includes adjacent communities and commercial centers that share mailing addresses, infrastructure, and [ZIP Codes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZIP_Code "ZIP Code") like 20147 and 20148. This includes communities such as [Brambleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brambleton,_Virginia "Brambleton, Virginia"), [Broadlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadlands,_Virginia "Broadlands, Virginia"), [Moorefield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moorefield,_Virginia "Moorefield, Virginia"), [Loudoun Valley Estates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_Valley_Estates,_Virginia "Loudoun Valley Estates, Virginia"), and [Belmont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belmont,_Virginia "Belmont, Virginia"). It originated as farmland and a small rail stop along the [Washington and Old Dominion railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_and_Old_Dominion_Railroad "Washington and Old Dominion Railroad"), gradually developing into a suburban area as transportation routes and regional growth pushed west from [Washington D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-11)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashburn,_Virginia&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

Ashburn, located in eastern [Loudoun County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_County,_Virginia "Loudoun County, Virginia"), Virginia, was originally part of a rural agricultural region known as Farmwell. The land was divided among several estates during the 18th and 19th centuries, forming part of the broader plantation economy that defined much of [northern Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Virginia "Northern Virginia"). During the [Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War "American Civil War"), [Loudoun County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_County,_Virginia "Loudoun County, Virginia") was deeply divided, and while Ashburn did not see major battles, it was affected by nearby troop movements, raids, and the broader regional instability at the time.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-ashburn-history-12)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/WASHINGTON_%26_OLD_DOMINION_R.R._CAR_EXTERIOR_LCCN2016861678.jpg/250px-WASHINGTON_%26_OLD_DOMINION_R.R._CAR_EXTERIOR_LCCN2016861678.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:WASHINGTON_&_OLD_DOMINION_R.R._CAR_EXTERIOR_LCCN2016861678.jpg)

Exterior of a cart on the Washington and Old Dominion Railroad

In the late 19th century, the arrival of the [Washington and Old Dominion Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_and_Old_Dominion_Railroad "Washington and Old Dominion Railroad") provided a transportation link that supported local farms and small industries, although Ashburn itself remained sparsely populated and primarily agricultural well into the 20th century. The [W&OD rail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_and_Old_Dominion_Railroad_Regional_Park "Washington and Old Dominion Railroad Regional Park") corridor, now a regional trail, is one of the area's key preserved historical routes. Following the [American Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War "American Civil War"), land ownership changed and farming practices shifted, but Ashburn continued to be defined by its rural character for many decades.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-13)

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Washington_Dulles_International_Airport_at_Dusk.jpg/250px-Washington_Dulles_International_Airport_at_Dusk.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Washington_Dulles_International_Airport_at_Dusk.jpg)

Main Terminal of Washington Dulles International Airport at dusk in Virginia, USA

Significant change began in the second half of the 20th century, particularly after the opening of [Washington Dulles International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport "Dulles International Airport") in 1962. This major infrastructure project spurred development throughout the surrounding region, and Ashburn's location made it a strategic site for future suburban and technological expansion. Major development in the 1980s and 1990s that came in the form of suburban neighborhoods and [planned communities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planned_communities "Planned communities") transformed the area into a major residential zone within [Northern Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Virginia "Northern Virginia")'s growing suburban region.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-14) By the early 2000s, Ashburn had become a hub for global internet infrastructure. A combination of reliable electricity and access to fiber-optic networks attracted major technology firms. The region developed the highest concentration of [data centers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_center "Data center") in the world, earning the nickname "Data Center Alley". Today, Ashburn is a central component of [Loudoun County's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_County,_Virginia "Loudoun County, Virginia") tech economy, supporting various technological industries in areas such as [cloud computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud_computing "Cloud computing") and [cybersecurity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cybersecurity "Cybersecurity") while also serving as a key residential area for workers in the greater [Washington, D.C. metro region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_metropolitan_area "Washington metropolitan area").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-15)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashburn,_Virginia&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Geography")]

Ashburn is located in eastern Loudoun County, 7 miles (11 km) southeast of [Leesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leesburg,_Virginia "Leesburg, Virginia"), the [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat"), and the same distance north of [Dulles International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport "Dulles International Airport"). As drawn by the [U.S. Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Census_Bureau "U.S. Census Bureau"), the area counted as "Ashburn" extends north to [Virginia State Route 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_State_Route_7 "Virginia State Route 7"), east to [Virginia State Route 28](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_State_Route_28 "Virginia State Route 28"), and southwest to the [Dulles Greenway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_Greenway "Dulles Greenway") (VA 267).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-TIGER-16) The Ashburn CDP is bordered to the north by the [Belmont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belmont,_Virginia "Belmont, Virginia"), [Lansdowne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lansdowne,_Virginia "Lansdowne, Virginia"), [One Loudoun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Loudoun "One Loudoun"), and [University Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_Center,_Virginia "University Center, Virginia") CDPs; to the east by the [Kincora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kincora,_Virginia "Kincora, Virginia"), [Dulles Town Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_Town_Center,_Virginia "Dulles Town Center, Virginia"), and [Sterling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sterling,_Virginia "Sterling, Virginia") CDPs; to the southwest by the [Moorefield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moorefield_Station,_Virginia "Moorefield Station, Virginia") and [Broadlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadlands,_Virginia "Broadlands, Virginia") CDPs; and to the west by the [Goose Creek Village](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goose_Creek_Village,_Virginia "Goose Creek Village, Virginia") CDP.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-TIGER-16)

According to the [2020 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the Ashburn CDP has a total area of 15.55 square miles (40.27 km 2), of which 15.30 square miles (39.63 km 2) are land and 0.25 square miles (0.65 km 2) are water.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-CenPopGazetteer2020-2) The area is drained by [Broad Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broad_Run_(Loudoun_County,_Virginia) "Broad Run (Loudoun County, Virginia)"), which flows northward through the eastern part of the CDP toward the [Potomac River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potomac_River "Potomac River").

## Economy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashburn,_Virginia&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Economy")]

Located within the [Dulles Technology Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_Technology_Corridor "Dulles Technology Corridor"), Ashburn is home to many high-tech businesses. World Trade Center Dulles Airport is the second [World Trade Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Centers_Association "World Trade Centers Association") in the state.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-WTC_-_Dulles_Airport_at_One_Loudoun-34)[Verizon Business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verizon_Business "Verizon Business") has a major office in Ashburn at the location replacing [MCI WorldCom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MCI_WorldCom "MCI WorldCom")'s headquarters after its acquisition.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-Verizon_Business_Global_Llc,_Verizon_Business-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-Telecom_Is_Getting_Another_Behemoth-36) Ashburn is also home to government contractor [Telos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telos_(company) "Telos (company)").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-37)

Ashburn is a major hub for [data centers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_center "Data center"), with companies such as [Digital Realty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Realty "Digital Realty"),[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-38)[Equinix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equinix "Equinix"),[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-39) and [NTT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NTT_Communications "NTT Communications"),[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-40) operating multiple facilities there.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-41) Among other websites, the [Wikimedia Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikimedia_Foundation "Wikimedia Foundation") (parent of Wikipedia) and [Amazon Web Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Web_Services "Amazon Web Services") have data centers there.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-45)

[Amazon Web Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Web_Services "Amazon Web Services") data center in Ashburn

The [George Washington University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington_University "George Washington University")'s Virginia Science and Technology Campus and the [Howard Hughes Medical Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Hughes_Medical_Institute "Howard Hughes Medical Institute")'s [Janelia Research Campus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janelia_Research_Campus "Janelia Research Campus") are located north of Ashburn in the University Center and Lansdowne CDPs, respectively. In 2026, the George Washington University sold their campus in Ashburn to [Amazon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_(company) "Amazon (company)") Data Services for over $400 million, which Amazon plans to use for the construction of a new data center.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-46) The BigBear.ai Performance Center, the training facility for the [Washington Commanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Commanders "Washington Commanders") of the [National Football League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Football_League "National Football League"), is located in the east part of Ashburn.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-The_Official_Site_of_the_Washington_Redskins-48)

[Airbus Group, Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airbus_Group,_Inc. "Airbus Group, Inc."), which is the North American affiliate of multinational aerospace corporation [Airbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airbus "Airbus"), and a large defense contractor, has a second location in Ashburn in addition to its main office in [Herndon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herndon,_Virginia "Herndon, Virginia"), Virginia.

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashburn,_Virginia&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Education")]

### Colleges and universities

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashburn,_Virginia&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Colleges and universities")]

[George Washington University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington_University "George Washington University") and [Strayer University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strayer_University "Strayer University") have campuses in the area. In December 2009, it was announced that [George Mason University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Mason_University "George Mason University") was planning to set up a campus in Ashburn, to be located at Exit 6 off the [Dulles Greenway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_Greenway "Dulles Greenway").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-49)

### Primary and secondary schools

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashburn,_Virginia&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Primary and secondary schools")]

Main article: [Loudoun County Public Schools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_County_Public_Schools "Loudoun County Public Schools")

Educational institutions in Ashburn are operated by the [Loudoun County Public Schools](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_County_Public_Schools "Loudoun County Public Schools").

Ashburn's elementary schools include Ashburn Elementary School, Belmont Station Elementary School, Cedar Lane Elementary School, Creighton's Corner Elementary, Discovery Elementary School, Dominion Trail Elementary School, Hillside Elementary School, Legacy Elementary School, Madison's Trust Elementary, Mill Run Elementary School, Moorefield Station Elementary School, Newton-Lee Elementary School, Rosa Lee Carter Elementary School, Sanders Corner Elementary School, Steuart W. Weller Elementary School, and Sycolin Creek Elementary School.

Ashburn's public middle schools include [Eagle Ridge Middle School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_County_Public_Schools "Loudoun County Public Schools"), [Farmwell Station Middle School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farmwell_Station_Middle_School "Farmwell Station Middle School"), Stone Hill Middle School, [Brambleton Middle School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brambleton_Middle_School "Brambleton Middle School"), Trailside Middle School, and Belmont Ridge Middle School.

Public high schools in Ashburn include [Briar Woods High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Briar_Woods_High_School "Briar Woods High School"), [Broad Run High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broad_Run_High_School "Broad Run High School"), [Independence High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independence_High_School_(Ashburn,_Virginia) "Independence High School (Ashburn, Virginia)"), [Rock Ridge High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_Ridge_High_School "Rock Ridge High School"), and [Stone Bridge High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stone_Bridge_High_School "Stone Bridge High School").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-Loudoun_County_Public_Schools:_Official_Website-50)

There are six private schools in Ashburn: [Loudoun School for Advanced Studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_School_for_Advanced_Studies "Loudoun School for Advanced Studies"), St. Theresa Catholic School, Virginia Academy, Leport School, The Loudoun Country Day School, and County Christian School.

## Infrastructure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashburn,_Virginia&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Infrastructure")]

### Washington Metro

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashburn,_Virginia&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Washington Metro")]

Ashburn is served by two [Washington Metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Metro "Washington Metro")[Silver Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Line_(Washington_Metro) "Silver Line (Washington Metro)") stations. After passing through Dulles Airport, the Silver Line enters Ashburn in the median of the [Dulles Greenway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_Greenway "Dulles Greenway").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-51) The first stop in Ashburn is [Loudoun Gateway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_Gateway_station "Loudoun Gateway station"), with [Ashburn station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn_station_(Washington_Metro) "Ashburn station (Washington Metro)") serving as the terminus. Originally planned to open in 2016, the opening was pushed back by multiple delays and finally opened on November 15, 2022.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-newsletter-nov-2012-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-53)

### Emergency services

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashburn,_Virginia&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Emergency services")]

Ashburn's fire and [emergency medical services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emergency_medical_services "Emergency medical services") are provided by the [Loudoun County Combined Fire and Rescue System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_County_Combined_Fire_and_Rescue_System "Loudoun County Combined Fire and Rescue System"). Ashburn Volunteer Fire and Rescue Department (AVFRD) is a volunteer company under LC-CFRS, and serves Ashburn with Stations 6 and 22, which are located near Inova Loudoun Hospital. LC-CFRS career staff operate Moorefield Station 23, near [Ashburn station (Washington Metro)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn_station_(Washington_Metro) "Ashburn station (Washington Metro)"). The Ashburn area is served by the Inova Ashburn Healthplex Emergency Room at the corner of the Dulles Greenway and Loudoun County Parkway as well as Inova Loudoun Hospital, located less than 2 miles (3.2 km) from Ashburn in neighboring [Lansdowne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lansdowne,_Virginia "Lansdowne, Virginia"), and by larger hospitals in the Washington suburbs and city.

**Ashburn** is an [unincorporated settlement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unincorporated_area#United_States "Unincorporated area") and [census-designated place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census-designated_place "Census-designated place") (CDP) in [Loudoun County, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_County,_Virginia "Loudoun County, Virginia"), United States. At the [2020 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), its population was 46,349,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-Census_2020-3) up from 3,393 in 1990. It is 30 miles (48 km) northwest of Washington, D.C., and part of the [Washington metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_metropolitan_area "Washington metropolitan area"). Ashburn is a major hub for [Internet traffic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internet_traffic "Internet traffic") due to its many [data centers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_center "Data center").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-6)

## Etymology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashburn,_Virginia&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Etymology")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8c/2018-10-25_14_33_59_View_west_along_Virginia_State_Route_267_%28Dulles_Greenway%29_at_Exit_5_%28Virginia_State_Route_901-Claiborne_Parkway%2C_Ashburn_Farm%2C_Broadlands%29_in_Broadlands%2C_Loudoun_County%2C_Virginia.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2018-10-25_14_33_59_View_west_along_Virginia_State_Route_267_(Dulles_Greenway)_at_Exit_5_(Virginia_State_Route_901-Claiborne_Parkway,_Ashburn_Farm,_Broadlands)_in_Broadlands,_Loudoun_County,_Virginia.jpg)

Dulles Greenway Exit 5 on to Claiborne Parkway toward Ashburn Farm

The name Ashburn is believed to have originated from "Ashburn Farm," a 1,236-acre estate originally owned by [John Janney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Janney "John Janney"), a prominent 19th-century [Quaker lawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quakers "Quakers") and politician who served as president of Virginia's Secession Convention in 1861. The property was later purchased by George Lee III in the 1870s, who is thought to have named it "Ashburn" either for the [ash trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fraxinus "Fraxinus") that dotted the landscape or possibly as a reference to the ash-colored soil or [barn fires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barn_fire "Barn fire") that had previously occurred in the area.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-7) Originally a quiet farming village known as Farmwell, the area became a part of a larger plantation economy in [Loudoun County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_County,_Virginia "Loudoun County, Virginia"). Ashburn remained largely rural through the early 20th century. It began to change significantly in the 1980s and 1990s with the expansion of the [Dulles Technology Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_Technology_Corridor "Dulles Technology Corridor") and the construction of large neighborhoods such as [Ashburn Village](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn_Village "Ashburn Village") and Ashburn Farm.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-8)

Today, Ashburn is a central part of [Loudoun County's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_County,_Virginia "Loudoun County, Virginia") high-tech economy and suburban expansion with preserved natural and historic landscapes such as the [W&OD Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_and_Old_Dominion_Railroad_Regional_Park "Washington and Old Dominion Railroad Regional Park") and nearby farms and battlefields.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-9)

According to the [US Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), Ashburn is a [census designated place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census-designated_place "Census-designated place"). Despite being restricted to a certain boundary, the broader "Ashburn area" includes adjacent communities and commercial centers that share mailing addresses, infrastructure, and [ZIP Codes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZIP_Code "ZIP Code") like 20147 and 20148. This includes communities such as [Brambleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brambleton,_Virginia "Brambleton, Virginia"), [Broadlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadlands,_Virginia "Broadlands, Virginia"), [Moorefield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moorefield,_Virginia "Moorefield, Virginia"), [Loudoun Valley Estates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_Valley_Estates,_Virginia "Loudoun Valley Estates, Virginia"), and [Belmont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belmont,_Virginia "Belmont, Virginia"). It originated as farmland and a small rail stop along the [Washington and Old Dominion railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_and_Old_Dominion_Railroad "Washington and Old Dominion Railroad"), gradually developing into a suburban area as transportation routes and regional growth pushed west from [Washington D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-11)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashburn,_Virginia&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

Ashburn, located in eastern [Loudoun County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_County,_Virginia "Loudoun County, Virginia"), Virginia, was originally part of a rural agricultural region known as Farmwell. The land was divided among several estates during the 18th and 19th centuries, forming part of the broader plantation economy that defined much of [northern Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Virginia "Northern Virginia"). During the [Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War "American Civil War"), [Loudoun County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_County,_Virginia "Loudoun County, Virginia") was deeply divided, and while Ashburn did not see major battles, it was affected by nearby troop movements, raids, and the broader regional instability at the time.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-ashburn-history-12)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/WASHINGTON_%26_OLD_DOMINION_R.R._CAR_EXTERIOR_LCCN2016861678.jpg/250px-WASHINGTON_%26_OLD_DOMINION_R.R._CAR_EXTERIOR_LCCN2016861678.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:WASHINGTON_&_OLD_DOMINION_R.R._CAR_EXTERIOR_LCCN2016861678.jpg)

Exterior of a cart on the Washington and Old Dominion Railroad

In the late 19th century, the arrival of the [Washington and Old Dominion Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_and_Old_Dominion_Railroad "Washington and Old Dominion Railroad") provided a transportation link that supported local farms and small industries, although Ashburn itself remained sparsely populated and primarily agricultural well into the 20th century. The [W&OD rail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_and_Old_Dominion_Railroad_Regional_Park "Washington and Old Dominion Railroad Regional Park") corridor, now a regional trail, is one of the area's key preserved historical routes. Following the [American Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War "American Civil War"), land ownership changed and farming practices shifted, but Ashburn continued to be defined by its rural character for many decades.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-13)

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Washington_Dulles_International_Airport_at_Dusk.jpg/250px-Washington_Dulles_International_Airport_at_Dusk.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Washington_Dulles_International_Airport_at_Dusk.jpg)

Main Terminal of Washington Dulles International Airport at dusk in Virginia, USA

Significant change began in the second half of the 20th century, particularly after the opening of [Washington Dulles International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport "Dulles International Airport") in 1962. This major infrastructure project spurred development throughout the surrounding region, and Ashburn's location made it a strategic site for future suburban and technological expansion. Major development in the 1980s and 1990s that came in the form of suburban neighborhoods and [planned communities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planned_communities "Planned communities") transformed the area into a major residential zone within [Northern Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Virginia "Northern Virginia")'s growing suburban region.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-14) By the early 2000s, Ashburn had become a hub for global internet infrastructure. A combination of reliable electricity and access to fiber-optic networks attracted major technology firms. The region developed the highest concentration of [data centers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_center "Data center") in the world, earning the nickname "Data Center Alley". Today, Ashburn is a central component of [Loudoun County's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_County,_Virginia "Loudoun County, Virginia") tech economy, supporting various technological industries in areas such as [cloud computing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud_computing "Cloud computing") and [cybersecurity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cybersecurity "Cybersecurity") while also serving as a key residential area for workers in the greater [Washington, D.C. metro region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_metropolitan_area "Washington metropolitan area").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-15)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashburn,_Virginia&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Geography")]

Ashburn is located in eastern Loudoun County, 7 miles (11 km) southeast of [Leesburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leesburg,_Virginia "Leesburg, Virginia"), the [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat"), and the same distance north of [Dulles International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_International_Airport "Dulles International Airport"). As drawn by the [U.S. Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Census_Bureau "U.S. Census Bureau"), the area counted as "Ashburn" extends north to [Virginia State Route 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_State_Route_7 "Virginia State Route 7"), east to [Virginia State Route 28](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_State_Route_28 "Virginia State Route 28"), and southwest to the [Dulles Greenway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_Greenway "Dulles Greenway") (VA 267).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-TIGER-16) The Ashburn CDP is bordered to the north by the [Belmont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belmont,_Virginia "Belmont, Virginia"), [Lansdowne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lansdowne,_Virginia "Lansdowne, Virginia"), [One Loudoun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Loudoun "One Loudoun"), and [University Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_Center,_Virginia "University Center, Virginia") CDPs; to the east by the [Kincora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kincora,_Virginia "Kincora, Virginia"), [Dulles Town Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_Town_Center,_Virginia "Dulles Town Center, Virginia"), and [Sterling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sterling,_Virginia "Sterling, Virginia") CDPs; to the southwest by the [Moorefield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moorefield_Station,_Virginia "Moorefield Station, Virginia") and [Broadlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadlands,_Virginia "Broadlands, Virginia") CDPs; and to the west by the [Goose Creek Village](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goose_Creek_Village,_Virginia "Goose Creek Village, Virginia") CDP.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-TIGER-16)

According to the [2020 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the Ashburn CDP has a total area of 15.55 square miles (40.27 km 2), of which 15.30 square miles (39.63 km 2) are land and 0.25 square miles (0.65 km 2) are water.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-CenPopGazetteer2020-2) The area is drained by [Broad Run](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broad_Run_(Loudoun_County,_Virginia) "Broad Run (Loudoun County, Virginia)"), which flows northward through the eastern part of the CDP toward the [Potomac River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potomac_River "Potomac River").

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashburn,_Virginia&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Ashburn had a population of 46,349. The median age was 39.7 years. 24.5% of residents were under the age of 18 and 15.1% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 93.2 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 88.8 males age 18 and over.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-Census2020PL-26)

100.0% of residents lived in urban areas, while 0.0% lived in rural areas.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-Census2020DHC-27)

There were 17,210 households in Ashburn, of which 36.9% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 58.5% were married-couple households, 12.7% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 25.1% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 24.7% of all households were made up of individuals and 12.1% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)

There were 17,906 housing units, of which 3.9% were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 0.4% and the rental vacancy rate was 8.2%.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-Census2020DP-25)

### Other demographics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashburn,_Virginia&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Other demographics")]

Many of its residents commute into Washington, D.C. and the surrounding suburbs such as [Tysons Corner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tysons_Corner "Tysons Corner") and [Reston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reston,_Virginia "Reston, Virginia") to their places of employment.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-Loudoun_County_Commuter_Bus_Adds_123_Spaces_for_Ashburn_Commuter_Parking-31) The median household income as of 2009 was $100,719.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-20147_Ashburn_Neighborhood_in_Ashburn,_VA-32) The median household size is 2.9 persons.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-20147_Ashburn_Neighborhood_in_Ashburn,_VA-32) 98% of Ashburn residents have a high school degree.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-20147_Ashburn_Neighborhood_in_Ashburn,_VA-32) Some 42 percent of Ashburn's population holds a four-year bachelor's degree;[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-20147_Ashburn_Neighborhood_in_Ashburn,_VA-32) 18 percent holds graduate degrees.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-20147_Ashburn_Neighborhood_in_Ashburn,_VA-32)

Homeowners formed 80% of the population,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-20147_Ashburn_Neighborhood_in_Ashburn,_VA-32) renters made up 13% of the population,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-20147_Ashburn_Neighborhood_in_Ashburn,_VA-32) and 7% of housing units were listed as vacancies.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-20147_Ashburn_Neighborhood_in_Ashburn,_VA-32) The median age of housing was 5.0 years.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-20147_Ashburn_Neighborhood_in_Ashburn,_VA-32) The median housing value is at $630,000.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-33)

## Economy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashburn,_Virginia&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Economy")]

Located within the [Dulles Technology Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_Technology_Corridor "Dulles Technology Corridor"), Ashburn is home to many high-tech businesses. World Trade Center Dulles Airport is the second [World Trade Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Centers_Association "World Trade Centers Association") in the state.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-WTC_-_Dulles_Airport_at_One_Loudoun-34)[Verizon Business](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Verizon_Business "Verizon Business") has a major office in Ashburn at the location replacing [MCI WorldCom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MCI_WorldCom "MCI WorldCom")'s headquarters after its acquisition.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-Verizon_Business_Global_Llc,_Verizon_Business-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-Telecom_Is_Getting_Another_Behemoth-36) Ashburn is also home to government contractor [Telos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telos_(company) "Telos (company)").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-37)

Ashburn is a major hub for [data centers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_center "Data center"), with companies such as [Digital Realty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Realty "Digital Realty"),[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-38)[Equinix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equinix "Equinix"),[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-39) and [NTT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NTT_Communications "NTT Communications"),[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-40) operating multiple facilities there.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-41) Among other websites, the [Wikimedia Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikimedia_Foundation "Wikimedia Foundation") (parent of Wikipedia) and [Amazon Web Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Web_Services "Amazon Web Services") have data centers there.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-45)

## Infrastructure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashburn,_Virginia&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Infrastructure")]

### Washington Metro

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashburn,_Virginia&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Washington Metro")]

Ashburn is served by two [Washington Metro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Metro "Washington Metro")[Silver Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silver_Line_(Washington_Metro) "Silver Line (Washington Metro)") stations. After passing through Dulles Airport, the Silver Line enters Ashburn in the median of the [Dulles Greenway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dulles_Greenway "Dulles Greenway").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-51) The first stop in Ashburn is [Loudoun Gateway station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_Gateway_station "Loudoun Gateway station"), with [Ashburn station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn_station_(Washington_Metro) "Ashburn station (Washington Metro)") serving as the terminus. Originally planned to open in 2016, the opening was pushed back by multiple delays and finally opened on November 15, 2022.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-newsletter-nov-2012-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn,_Virginia#cite_note-53)

### Emergency services

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ashburn,_Virginia&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Emergency services")]

Ashburn's fire and [emergency medical services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emergency_medical_services "Emergency medical services") are provided by the [Loudoun County Combined Fire and Rescue System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudoun_County_Combined_Fire_and_Rescue_System "Loudoun County Combined Fire and Rescue System"). Ashburn Volunteer Fire and Rescue Department (AVFRD) is a volunteer company under LC-CFRS, and serves Ashburn with Stations 6 and 22, which are located near Inova Loudoun Hospital. LC-CFRS career staff operate Moorefield Station 23, near [Ashburn station (Washington Metro)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashburn_station_(Washington_Metro) "Ashburn station (Washington Metro)"). The Ashburn area is served by the Inova Ashburn Healthplex Emergency Room at the corner of the Dulles Greenway and Loudoun County Parkway as well as Inova Loudoun Hospital, located less than 2 miles (3.2 km) from Ashburn in neighboring [Lansdowne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lansdowne,_Virginia "Lansdowne, Virginia"), and by larger hospitals in the Washington suburbs and city.
