**Henry Clay** (April 12, 1777–June 29, 1852) was an American lawyer, statesman, and diplomat who represented [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky "Kentucky") in both the [United States House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") and the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate"). He was the seventh [House speaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speaker_of_the_United_States_House_of_Representatives "Speaker of the United States House of Representatives") as well as the ninth [secretary of state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State "United States Secretary of State"). Clay unsuccessfully ran for president in the [1824](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1824_United_States_presidential_election "1824 United States presidential election"), [1832](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1832_United_States_presidential_election "1832 United States presidential election"), and [1844](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1844_United_States_presidential_election "1844 United States presidential election") elections. He helped found both the [National Republican Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Republican_Party "National Republican Party") and the [Whig Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whig_Party_(United_States) "Whig Party (United States)"). For his role in defusing [sectional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sectionalism "Sectionalism") crises, he earned the appellation of the "**Great Compromiser**" and was part of the "[Great Triumvirate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Triumvirate "Great Triumvirate")" of Congressmen, alongside fellow Whig [Daniel Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Webster "Daniel Webster") and [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)")[John C. Calhoun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_C._Calhoun "John C. Calhoun").

Clay was born in [Hanover County, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanover_County,_Virginia "Hanover County, Virginia"), in 1777, and began his legal career in [Lexington, Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexington,_Kentucky "Lexington, Kentucky"), in 1797. As a member of the [Democratic-Republican Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic-Republican_Party "Democratic-Republican Party"), he won election to the Kentucky state legislature in 1803 and to the U.S. House of Representatives in 1810. Clay was chosen as Speaker of the House in early 1811 and, along with President [James Madison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Madison "James Madison"), led the United States into the [War of 1812](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_1812 "War of 1812") against Great Britain. In 1814, he helped negotiate the [Treaty of Ghent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Ghent "Treaty of Ghent"), which brought an end to the War of 1812, and then after the war, Clay returned to his position as Speaker of the House and developed the [American System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_System_(economic_plan) "American System (economic plan)"), which called for federal [infrastructure investments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_improvements "Internal improvements"), support for the [national bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_central_banking_in_the_United_States "History of central banking in the United States"), and high protective [tariff rates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tariff_in_United_States_history "Tariff in United States history"). During 1820, Clay helped bring an end to a sectional crisis over [slavery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery_in_the_United_States "Slavery in the United States") for many years by leading the passage of the [Missouri Compromise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Compromise "Missouri Compromise"). He finished with the fourth-most electoral votes in the multi-candidate [1824–1825 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1824_United_States_presidential_election "1824 United States presidential election") and used his position as speaker to help [John Quincy Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Quincy_Adams "John Quincy Adams") win the [contingent election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contingent_election "Contingent election") held to select the president. President Adams then appointed him to the position of Secretary of State. As a result, critics alleged that the two had agreed to a "[corrupt bargain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Corrupt_Bargain "First Corrupt Bargain")".

Adams was defeated by Democrat [Andrew Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Jackson "Andrew Jackson") in the bitter [1828 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1828_United_States_presidential_election "1828 United States presidential election"). Clay won election to the U.S. Senate in 1831 and ran as the National Republican nominee in the 1832 presidential election. Clay was defeated decisively by President Jackson primarily due to his support for the [national bank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_War "Bank War"), which Jackson vehemently opposed. After the 1832 election, Clay helped bring an end to the [nullification crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nullification_crisis "Nullification crisis") by leading passage of the [Tariff of 1833](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tariff_of_1833 "Tariff of 1833"). During Jackson's second term, opponents of the president including Clay, Webster, and [William Henry Harrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Henry_Harrison "William Henry Harrison") created the Whig Party, and Clay became a leading congressional Whig.

Clay sought the presidency in the [1840 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1840_United_States_presidential_election "1840 United States presidential election") but was passed over at the [Whig National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1839_Whig_National_Convention "1839 Whig National Convention") in favor of Harrison. When Harrison died and his vice president [John Tyler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Tyler "John Tyler") ascended to office in 1841, Clay clashed with Tyler, who broke with Clay and other congressional Whigs. Clay resigned from the Senate in 1842 and won the 1844 Whig presidential nomination, but he was narrowly defeated in the general election by Democrat [James K. Polk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_K._Polk "James K. Polk"), who made the annexation of the [Republic of Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Texas "Republic of Texas") his top issue. Clay strongly criticized the subsequent [Mexican–American War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican%E2%80%93American_War "Mexican–American War"), where his son [Henry Clay Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay_Jr. "Henry Clay Jr.") was killed at the [Battle of Buena Vista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Buena_Vista "Battle of Buena Vista"), and sought the Whig presidential nomination in [1848](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1848_United_States_presidential_election "1848 United States presidential election") but was passed over in favor of General [Zachary Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zachary_Taylor "Zachary Taylor") who went on to win the election. After returning to the Senate in 1849, Clay played a key role in passing the [Compromise of 1850](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compromise_of_1850 "Compromise of 1850"), which postponed a crisis over the status of slavery in the territories.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Henry_Clay&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Henry Clay was born on April 12, 1777, at the Clay homestead in [Hanover County, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanover_County,_Virginia "Hanover County, Virginia").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEaton19575-1) He was the seventh of nine children born to the Reverend John Clay and Elizabeth (née Hudson) Clay.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEVan_Deusen19374-2) Almost all of Henry's older siblings died before adulthood.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-:2-3) His father, a [Baptist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baptists "Baptists") minister nicknamed "Sir John", died in 1781, leaving Henry and his brothers two enslaved individuals each; he also left his wife 18 slaves and 464 acres (188 ha) of land.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEaton19576%E2%80%937-4) Clay was of entirely [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_Americans "English Americans") descent;[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTERemini1991xxiv,_4-5) his ancestor, John Clay, settled in Virginia in 1613.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler20104%E2%80%935-6) The [Clay family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clay_family "Clay family") became a well-known political family including three other US senators, numerous state politicians, and Clay's cousin [Cassius Clay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassius_Marcellus_Clay_(politician) "Cassius Marcellus Clay (politician)"), a prominent anti-slavery activist active in the mid-19th century.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter2018309-7)

The British raided Clay's home shortly after the death of his father, leaving the family in a precarious economic position.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler20109%E2%80%9310-8) However, the widow Elizabeth Clay married Captain Henry Watkins, a successful [planter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planter_class "Planter class") and cousin to John Clay.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201011%E2%80%9313-9) Elizabeth would have seven more children with Watkins, bearing a total of sixteen children.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEaton19576-10) Watkins became a kind and supportive stepfather and Clay had a very good relationship with him.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-11) After his mother's remarriage, the young Clay remained in Hanover County, where he learned how to read and write.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201011%E2%80%9313-9) In 1791, Watkins moved the family to Kentucky, joining his brother in the pursuit of fertile new lands in the West. However, Clay did not follow, as Watkins secured his temporary employment in a [Richmond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond,_Virginia "Richmond, Virginia") emporium, with the promise that Clay would receive the next available clerkship at the [Virginia Court of Chancery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Court_of_Chancery "Virginia Court of Chancery").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201013%E2%80%9315-12)

After Clay had worked at the Richmond emporium for a year, he obtained a clerkship that had become available at the Virginia Court of Chancery. Clay adapted well to his new role, and his handwriting earned him the attention of [College of William & Mary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_of_William_&_Mary "College of William & Mary") professor [George Wythe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Wythe "George Wythe"), a signer of the [Declaration of Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Declaration_of_Independence "United States Declaration of Independence"), mentor of [Thomas Jefferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson"), and judge on Virginia's High Court of Chancery.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201019%E2%80%9320-13) Hampered by a crippled hand, Wythe chose Clay as his secretary and [amanuensis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanuensis "Amanuensis"), a role in which Clay would remain for four years.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEaton19577-14) Clay began to [read law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reading_law "Reading law") under Wythe's mentorship.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-15) Wythe had a powerful effect on Clay's worldview, with Clay embracing Wythe's belief that the example of the United States could help spread human freedom around the world.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201020%E2%80%9321-16) Wythe subsequently arranged a position for Clay with Virginia attorney general [Robert Brooke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Brooke_(Virginia_governor) "Robert Brooke (Virginia governor)"), with the understanding that Brooke would finish Clay's legal studies.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201023-17) After completing his studies under Brooke, Clay was [admitted to the Virginia Bar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Admission_to_the_bar_in_the_United_States "Admission to the bar in the United States") in 1797.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter20185-18)

## Marriage and family

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Henry_Clay&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Marriage and family")]

See also: [Clay family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clay_family "Clay family")

On April 11, 1799, Clay married Lucretia Hart (1781–1864) at the Hart home in [Lexington, Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexington,_Kentucky "Lexington, Kentucky"). Her father, Colonel Thomas Hart, was an early settler of Kentucky and a prominent businessman.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEaton195712-19) Hart proved to be an important business connection for Clay, as he helped Clay gain new clients and grow in professional stature.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201041%E2%80%9342-20) Hart was the namesake and grand-uncle of Missouri Senator [Thomas Hart Benton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Hart_Benton_(politician) "Thomas Hart Benton (politician)") and was also related to [James Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Brown_(Louisiana_politician) "James Brown (Louisiana politician)"), a prominent Louisiana politician, and [Isaac Shelby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaac_Shelby "Isaac Shelby"), the first [governor of Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Kentucky "Governor of Kentucky").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter201812%E2%80%9313-21) Henry Clay was an active Freemason, and served as worshipful master of Lexington lodge No.1 in 1801. Henry and Lucretia would remain married until his death in 1852; she lived until 1864, dying at the age of 83. Both are buried at [Lexington Cemetery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lexington_Cemetery "Lexington Cemetery").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-22)

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/79/Henry_Clay_and_wife_%28cropped%29.tif/lossy-page1-250px-Henry_Clay_and_wife_%28cropped%29.tif.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Henry_Clay_and_wife_(cropped).tif)

Henry Clay and Lucretia ([née](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_name#Maiden_and_married_names "Birth name")Hart)

Clay and Lucretia had eleven children (six daughters and five sons):[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-Gatton-23) Henrietta (born in 1800), Theodore (1802), Thomas (1803), Susan (1805), Anne (1807), Lucretia (1809), [Henry Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay_Jr. "Henry Clay Jr.") (1811), Eliza (1813), Laura (1815), [James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Brown_Clay "James Brown Clay") (1817), and [John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Morrison_Clay "John Morrison Clay") (1821). By 1835, all six daughters had died of varying causes, two when very young, two as children, and the last two as young mothers. Henry Jr. was killed while commanding a regiment at the [Battle of Buena Vista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Buena_Vista "Battle of Buena Vista") during the [Mexican–American War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican%E2%80%93American_War "Mexican–American War"). Clay's oldest son, Theodore Wythe Clay, spent the second half of his life confined to a [psychiatric hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychiatric_hospital "Psychiatric hospital"). When a young child, Theodore was injured by a blow to his head that fractured his skull. As he grew older his condition devolved into insanity, and from 1831 until his death in 1870 he was confined to [an asylum in Lexington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_State_Hospital_(Kentucky) "Eastern State Hospital (Kentucky)").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-Gatton-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010402-24) Thomas (who had served some jail time in Philadelphia in 1829–1830)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-Gatton-23) became a successful farmer, James established a legal practice (and later served in Congress), and John (who in his mid-20s was also confined to the asylum for a short time) became a successful horse breeder.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter2018285%E2%80%93286-25)

Clay was greatly interested in gambling, although he favored numerous restrictions and legal limitations on it. Famously, he once won $40,000 (approximately $970,000 as of 2020).[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-26) Clay asked for $500 (approximately $12,000 today) and waived the remainder of the debt. Shortly afterward, Clay fell into a debt of $60,000 (approximately $1.5 million today[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-27)) while gambling with the same man, who then asked for the $500 back and waived the rest of the debt.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-28)

They initially lived in Lexington, but in 1804 they began building a [plantation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plantation_complexes_in_the_Southern_United_States "Plantation complexes in the Southern United States") outside of Lexington known as [Ashland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashland_(Henry_Clay_estate) "Ashland (Henry Clay estate)"). The Ashland estate eventually encompassed over 500 acres (200 ha), with numerous outbuildings such as a smokehouse, a greenhouse, and several barns. There were 122 enslaved people at the estate during Clay's lifetime, with about 50 people needed for farming and the household.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-:1-29) He planted crops such as corn, wheat, and rye, as well as [hemp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemp "Hemp"), the chief crop of the [Bluegrass region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluegrass_region "Bluegrass region").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter2018275%E2%80%93277-30) Clay also took a strong interest in [thoroughbred racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoroughbred_racing "Thoroughbred racing") and imported livestock such as [Arabian horses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_horse "Arabian horse"), [Maltese donkeys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maltese_donkey "Maltese donkey"), and [Hereford cattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hereford_cattle "Hereford cattle").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter2018277%E2%80%93278-31) Though Clay suffered some financial issues during economic downturns, he never fell deeply into debt and ultimately left his children a large inheritance.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter2018279%E2%80%93280-32) After the deaths of Anne and Susan, Clay and Lucretia raised several grandchildren at Ashland.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter2018288-33)

## Early career in law and politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Henry_Clay&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early career in law and politics")]

### Legal career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Henry_Clay&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Legal career")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Henry_Clay%27s_law_office.jpg/250px-Henry_Clay%27s_law_office.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Henry_Clay's_law_office.jpg)

View of Henry Clay's law office (1803–1810), Lexington, Kentucky

In November 1797, Clay relocated to Lexington, Kentucky, near where his parents and siblings resided. The Bluegrass region, with Lexington at its center, had quickly grown in the preceding decades but had only recently stopped being under the threat of [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") raids. Lexington was an established town that hosted [Transylvania University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transylvania_University "Transylvania University"), the first university west of the [Appalachian Mountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appalachian_Mountains "Appalachian Mountains").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201027%E2%80%9329-34) Having already passed the Virginia Bar, Clay quickly received a Kentucky license to practice law. After apprenticing himself to Kentucky attorneys such as [George Nicholas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Nicholas_(politician) "George Nicholas (politician)"), [John Breckenridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Breckinridge_(U.S._Attorney_General) "John Breckinridge (U.S. Attorney General)"), and James Brown, Clay established his own law practice, frequently working on debt collections and land disputes.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201030%E2%80%9331-35) Clay soon established a reputation for strong legal ability and courtroom oratory. In 1805, he was appointed to the faculty of Transylvania University where he taught, among others, future Kentucky Governor [Robert P. Letcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_P._Letcher "Robert P. Letcher") and Robert Todd, the future father-in-law of [Abraham Lincoln](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln "Abraham Lincoln").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201043-36)

Clay's client [Aaron Burr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Burr "Aaron Burr") was indicted for treason in the [Burr conspiracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burr_conspiracy "Burr conspiracy"). Clay and his law partner [John Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Allen_(soldier) "John Allen (soldier)") successfully defended Burr without charging a fee in 1807.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-37)[Thomas Jefferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson") later convinced Clay that Burr had been guilty of the charges.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEaton195715-38) Clay's legal practice was light after his election to Congress. In the 1823 case _[Green v. Biddle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green\_v.\_Biddle "Green v. Biddle")_, Clay submitted the [Supreme Court's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "Supreme Court of the United States") first [amicus curiae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amicus_curiae "Amicus curiae"). However, he lost that case.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-39)

### Early political career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Henry_Clay&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Early political career")]

Further information: [9th United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9th_United_States_Congress "9th United States Congress") and [11th United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/11th_United_States_Congress "11th United States Congress")

Clay entered politics shortly after arriving in Kentucky. In his first political speech, he attacked the [Alien and Sedition Acts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alien_and_Sedition_Acts "Alien and Sedition Acts"), laws passed by Federalists to suppress dissent during the [Quasi-War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quasi-War "Quasi-War") with France.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter201820%E2%80%9321-40) Like most Kentuckians, Clay was a member of the [Democratic-Republican Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic-Republican_Party "Democratic-Republican Party"), but he clashed with state party leaders over a state constitutional convention. Using the pseudonym "Scaevola" (in reference to [Gaius Mucius Scaevola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaius_Mucius_Scaevola "Gaius Mucius Scaevola")), Clay advocated for direct elections for Kentucky elected officials and the [gradual emancipation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradual_emancipation_(United_States) "Gradual emancipation (United States)") of [slavery in Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_slavery_in_Kentucky "History of slavery in Kentucky"). The 1799 [Kentucky Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_Kentucky "Constitution of Kentucky") included the direct election of public officials, but the state did not adopt Clay's plan for gradual emancipation.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201033%E2%80%9336-41)

In 1803, Clay won election to the [Kentucky House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_House_of_Representatives "Kentucky House of Representatives").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter201821%E2%80%9323-42) His first legislative initiative was the partisan [gerrymander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerrymandering_in_the_United_States "Gerrymandering in the United States") of Kentucky's [Electoral College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Electoral_College "United States Electoral College") districts, which ensured that all of Kentucky's presidential electors voted for President Jefferson in the [1804 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1804_United_States_presidential_election "1804 United States presidential election").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201048%E2%80%9351-43) Clay clashed with legislators who sought to reduce the power of Clay's Bluegrass region, and he unsuccessfully advocated moving the state capitol from [Frankfort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankfort,_Kentucky "Frankfort, Kentucky") to Lexington. Clay frequently opposed populist firebrand [Felix Grundy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felix_Grundy "Felix Grundy"), and he helped defeat Grundy's effort to revoke the banking privileges of the state-owned Kentucky Insurance Company. He advocated for the construction of [internal improvements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_improvements "Internal improvements"), which would become a consistent theme throughout his public career.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201048%E2%80%9351-43) Clay's influence in Kentucky state politics was such that in 1806 the Kentucky legislature elected him to the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter201825%E2%80%9326-44)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-47) During his two-month tenure in the Senate, Clay advocated for the construction of various bridges and canals, including [a canal connecting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chesapeake_&_Delaware_Canal "Chesapeake & Delaware Canal") the [Chesapeake Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chesapeake_Bay "Chesapeake Bay") and the [Delaware River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delaware_River "Delaware River").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201064%E2%80%9367-48)

After Clay returned to Kentucky in 1807, he was elected as the speaker of the state house of representatives.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter201810%E2%80%9310-49) That same year, in response to attacks on American shipping by Britain and France during the [Napoleonic Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleonic_Wars "Napoleonic Wars"), President Jefferson arranged passage of the [Embargo Act of 1807](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embargo_Act_of_1807 "Embargo Act of 1807"). In support of Jefferson's policy, which limited trade with foreign powers, Clay introduced a resolution to require legislators to wear [homespun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinning_(textiles) "Spinning (textiles)") suits rather than those made of imported British [broadcloth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadcloth "Broadcloth").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201070%E2%80%9371-50) The vast majority of members of the state house voted for the measure, but [Humphrey Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humphrey_Marshall_(politician) "Humphrey Marshall (politician)"), an "aristocratic lawyer who possessed a sarcastic tongue," voted against it.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEaton195717-51) In early 1809, Clay challenged Marshall to a [duel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dueling_in_the_Southern_United_States "Dueling in the Southern United States"), which took place on January 19.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTERemini199155-52) While many contemporary duels were called off or fought without the intention of killing one another, both Clay and Marshall fought the duel with the intent of killing their opponent.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201072%E2%80%9373-53) They each had three turns to shoot; both were hit by bullets, but both survived.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEaton195717-51) Clay quickly recovered from his injury and received only a minor [censure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Censure "Censure") from the Kentucky legislature.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201074-54)

In 1810, U.S. Senator [Buckner Thruston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buckner_Thruston "Buckner Thruston") resigned to accept appointment to a position as a federal judge, and Clay was selected by the legislature to fill Thruston's seat. Clay quickly emerged as a fierce critic of British attacks on American shipping, becoming part of an informal group of "[war hawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_hawk "War hawk")" who favored expansionist policies.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter201826%E2%80%9330-55) He also advocated the annexation of [West Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Florida "West Florida"), which was controlled by Spain.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201079%E2%80%9381-56) On the insistence of the Kentucky legislature, Clay helped prevent the re-charter of the [First Bank of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Bank_of_the_United_States "First Bank of the United States"), arguing that it interfered with state banks and infringed on [states' rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States'_rights "States' rights").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201081%E2%80%9383-57) After serving in the Senate for one year, Clay decided that he disliked the rules of the Senate and instead sought election to the [United States House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201076%E2%80%9378-58) He won election unopposed in late 1810.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter201830-59)

## Speaker of the House

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Henry_Clay&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Speaker of the House")]

### Election and leadership

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Henry_Clay&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Election and leadership")]

The [1810–1811 elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1810_and_1811_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections "1810 and 1811 United States House of Representatives elections") produced many young, anti-British members of Congress who, like Clay, supported going to war with Great Britain. Buoyed by the support of fellow [war hawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_hawk "War hawk"), Clay was elected [Speaker of the House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speaker_of_the_United_States_House_of_Representatives "Speaker of the United States House of Representatives") for the [12th Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12th_United_States_Congress "12th United States Congress").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201085-60) At 34, he was the youngest person to become speaker, a distinction he held until 1839, when 30-year-old [Robert M. T. Hunter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_M._T._Hunter "Robert M. T. Hunter") took office.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-61) He was also the first of only two new members elected speaker to date,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-62) the other being [William Pennington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Pennington "William Pennington") in 1860.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-63)

Between 1810 and 1824, Clay was elected to seven terms in the House.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-64) His tenure was interrupted from 1814 to 1815 when he was a commissioner to peace talks with the British in [Ghent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghent "Ghent"), [United Netherlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sovereign_Principality_of_the_United_Netherlands "Sovereign Principality of the United Netherlands") to end the [War of 1812](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_1812 "War of 1812"), and from 1821 to 1823, when he left Congress to rebuild his family's fortune in the aftermath of the [Panic of 1819](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panic_of_1819 "Panic of 1819").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010148%E2%80%93149-65)[Elected speaker six times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Speaker_of_the_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections "List of Speaker of the United States House of Representatives elections"), Clay's cumulative tenure in office of 10 years, 196 days, is the second-longest, surpassed only by [Sam Rayburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Rayburn "Sam Rayburn").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-66)

As speaker, Clay wielded considerable power in making committee appointments, and like many of his predecessors he assigned his allies to important committees. Clay was exceptional in his ability to control the legislative agenda through well-placed allies and the establishment of new committees and departed from precedent by frequently taking part in floor debates.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201086-67) Yet he also gained a reputation for personal courteousness and fairness in his rulings and committee appointments.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter201831%E2%80%9332-68) Clay's drive to increase the power of the office of speaker was aided by President [James Madison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Madison "James Madison"), who deferred to Congress in most matters.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201088%E2%80%9389-69)[John Randolph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Randolph_of_Roanoke "John Randolph of Roanoke"), a member of the Democratic-Republican Party but also a member of the "[tertium quids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tertium_quids "Tertium quids")" group that opposed many federal initiatives, emerged as a prominent opponent of Speaker Clay.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201087%E2%80%9388-70) While Randolph frequently attempted to obstruct Clay's initiatives, Clay became a master of parliamentary maneuvers that enabled him to advance his agenda even over the attempted obstruction by Randolph and others.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201096-71)[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-73)

### Madison administration, 1811–1817

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Henry_Clay&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Madison administration, 1811–1817")]

Further information: [Presidency of James Madison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_James_Madison "Presidency of James Madison"), [12th United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/12th_United_States_Congress "12th United States Congress"), [13th United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/13th_United_States_Congress "13th United States Congress"), and [14th United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/14th_United_States_Congress "14th United States Congress")

Clay and others he sided with demanded that the British revoke the [Orders in Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orders_in_Council_(1807) "Orders in Council (1807)"), a series of decrees that had resulted in a de facto commercial war with the United States.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201089%E2%80%9390-74) Though Clay recognized the dangers inherent in fighting Britain, one of the most powerful countries in the world, he saw it as the only realistic alternative to a humiliating submission to British attacks on American shipping.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter201833-75) Clay led a successful effort in the House to [declare war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_of_war_by_the_United_States "Declaration of war by the United States") against Britain, complying with a request from President Madison.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201097%E2%80%9398-76) Madison signed the declaration of war on June 18, 1812, beginning the War of 1812. During the war, Clay frequently communicated with Secretary of State [James Monroe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Monroe "James Monroe") and Secretary of War [William Eustis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Eustis "William Eustis"), though he advocated for the replacement of the latter.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201099%E2%80%93101-77) The war started poorly for the Americans, and Clay lost friends and relatives in the fighting.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler201097%E2%80%9398-76) In October 1813, the British asked Madison to begin negotiations in Europe, and Madison asked Clay to join his diplomatic team, as the president hoped that the presence of the leading war hawk would ensure support for a peace treaty. Clay was reluctant to leave Congress but felt duty-bound to accept the offer, and so he resigned from Congress on January 19, 1814.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010107%E2%80%93108-78)

Clay left the country on February 25, but negotiations with the British did not begin until August 1814. Clay was part of a team of five commissioners that included Treasury Secretary [Albert Gallatin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Gallatin "Albert Gallatin"), Senator [James Bayard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_A._Bayard_(elder) "James A. Bayard (elder)"), ambassador [Jonathan Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Russell_(diplomat) "Jonathan Russell (diplomat)"), and ambassador [John Quincy Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Quincy_Adams "John Quincy Adams"), the head of the American team.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-79) Clay and Adams maintained an uneasy relationship marked by frequent clashes, and Gallatin emerged as the unofficial leader of the American team. When the British finally presented their initial peace offer, Clay was outraged by its terms, especially the British proposal for an [Indian barrier state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_barrier_state "Indian barrier state") on the [Great Lakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Lakes "Great Lakes"). After a series of American military successes in 1814, the British delegation made several concessions and offered a better peace deal.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010110%E2%80%93117-80) While Adams and Gallatin were eager to make peace as quickly as possible even if that required sub-optimal terms in the peace treaty, Clay believed that the British, worn down by years of fighting against France, greatly desired peace with the United States. Partly due to Clay's hard-line stance, the [Treaty of Ghent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Ghent "Treaty of Ghent") included relatively favorable terms for the United States, essentially re-establishing the _[status quo ante bellum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Status\_quo\_ante\_bellum "Status quo ante bellum")_ between Britain and the U.S. The treaty was signed on December 24, 1814, bringing a close to the War of 1812.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter201835%E2%80%9336-81) After the signing of the treaty, Clay briefly traveled to London, where he helped Gallatin negotiate a commercial agreement with Britain.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010117-82)

Clay returned to the United States in September 1815; despite his absence, he had been elected to another term in the House of Representatives. Upon his return to Congress, Clay won election as Speaker of the House.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010119%E2%80%93122-83) The War of 1812 strengthened Clay's support for interventionist economic policies such as federally funded internal improvements, which he believed were necessary to improve the country's infrastructure system.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter201839%E2%80%9340-84) He eagerly embraced President Madison's ambitious domestic package, which included infrastructure investment, [tariffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tariff_in_United_States_history "Tariff in United States history") to [protect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protective_tariff "Protective tariff") domestic manufacturing, and spending increases for the army and navy. With the help of [John C. Calhoun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_C._Calhoun "John C. Calhoun") and [William Lowndes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Lowndes_(congressman) "William Lowndes (congressman)"), Clay passed the [Tariff of 1816](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tariff_of_1816 "Tariff of 1816"), which served the dual purpose of raising revenue and protecting American manufacturing. To stabilize the currency, Clay and Treasury Secretary [Alexander Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_J._Dallas_(statesman) "Alexander J. Dallas (statesman)") arranged passage of a bill establishing the [Second Bank of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Bank_of_the_United_States "Second Bank of the United States") (also known as the national bank).[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010123%E2%80%93131-85) Clay also supported the [Bonus Bill of 1817](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonus_Bill_of_1817 "Bonus Bill of 1817"), which would have provided a fund for internal improvements, but Madison vetoed the bill on constitutional concerns.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010132%E2%80%93133-86) Beginning in 1818, Clay advocated for an economic plan known as the "[American System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_System_(economic_plan) "American System (economic plan)")", which encompassed many of the economic measures, including protective tariffs and infrastructure investments, that he helped pass in the aftermath of the War of 1812.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter201881%E2%80%9382-87)

### Monroe administration, 1817–1825

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Henry_Clay&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Monroe administration, 1817–1825")]

Further information: [Presidency of James Monroe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_James_Monroe "Presidency of James Monroe"), [15th United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15th_United_States_Congress "15th United States Congress"), [16th United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16th_United_States_Congress "16th United States Congress"), [17th United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/17th_United_States_Congress "17th United States Congress"), and [18th United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/18th_United_States_Congress "18th United States Congress")

Like Jefferson and [George Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Washington "George Washington"), President Madison decided to retire after two terms, leaving open the Democratic-Republican nomination for the [1816 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1816_United_States_presidential_election "1816 United States presidential election"). At the time, the Democratic-Republicans used a [congressional nominating caucus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congressional_nominating_caucus "Congressional nominating caucus") to choose their presidential nominees, giving congressmen a powerful role in the presidential selection process. Monroe and Secretary of War [William Crawford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_H._Crawford "William H. Crawford") emerged as the two main candidates for the Democratic-Republican nomination. Clay had a favorable opinion of both individuals, but he supported Monroe, who won the nomination and went on to defeat Federalist candidate [Rufus King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rufus_King "Rufus King") in the general election.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010126%E2%80%93130-88) Monroe offered Clay the position of secretary of war, but Clay strongly desired the office of secretary of state and was angered when Monroe instead chose John Quincy Adams for that position.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter201840%E2%80%9341-89) Clay became so bitter that he refused to allow Monroe's inauguration to take place in the House Chamber and subsequently did not attend Monroe's outdoor inauguration.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTERemini1991150%E2%80%93151-90)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Henry_Clay.JPG/250px-Henry_Clay.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Henry_Clay.JPG)

Portrait by [Matthew Harris Jouett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_Harris_Jouett "Matthew Harris Jouett"), 1818

In early 1819, a dispute erupted over the proposed statehood of [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri") after New York Congressman [James Tallmadge Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Tallmadge_Jr. "James Tallmadge Jr.") introduced a [legislative amendment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tallmadge_Amendment "Tallmadge Amendment") that would provide for the gradual emancipation of Missouri's enslaved people.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter201844%E2%80%9345-91) Though Clay had previously called for gradual emancipation in Kentucky, he sided with fellow Southerners in voting down Tallmadge's amendment.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010143%E2%80%93144-92) Clay instead supported Illinois Senator [Jesse B. Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_B._Thomas "Jesse B. Thomas")'s compromise proposal in which Missouri would be admitted as a [slave state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slave_states_and_free_states "Slave states and free states"), [Maine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine "Maine") would be admitted as a free state,[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-93) and slavery would be forbidden in the territories north of 36° 30' parallel. Clay helped assemble a coalition that passed the [Missouri Compromise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Compromise "Missouri Compromise"), as Thomas's proposal became known.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter201845%E2%80%9346-94) Further controversy ensued when Missouri's constitution banned free blacks from entering the state, but Clay was able to engineer another compromise that allowed Missouri to join as a state in August 1821.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010150%E2%80%93152-95)

In foreign policy, Clay was a leading American supporter of the [independence movements and revolutions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decolonization_of_the_Americas "Decolonization of the Americas") that broke out in [Latin America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_America "Latin America") beginning in 1810.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter201874%E2%80%9375-96) Clay frequently called on the Monroe administration to recognize the fledgling Latin American republics, but Monroe feared that doing so would derail his plans to acquire [Spanish Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Florida "Spanish Florida").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010136%E2%80%93137-97) In 1818, General [Andrew Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Jackson "Andrew Jackson") crossed into Spanish Florida to suppress raids by [Seminole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seminole "Seminole") Indians.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010137%E2%80%93138-98) Though Jackson was following Monroe's implied wishes in entering Florida, he created additional controversy in seizing the Spanish town of [Pensacola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pensacola,_Florida "Pensacola, Florida"). Despite protests from Secretary of War Calhoun, Monroe and Adams decided to support Jackson's actions in the hope that they would convince Spain to sell Florida.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010137%E2%80%93138-98) Clay, however, was outraged, and he publicly condemned Jackson's [decision to hang two foreign nationals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arbuthnot_and_Ambrister_incident "Arbuthnot and Ambrister incident") without a trial. Before the House chamber, he compared Jackson to military dictators of the past, telling his colleagues "that Greece had her [Alexander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_the_Great "Alexander the Great"), [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Rome "Ancient Rome") her [Caesar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julius_Caesar "Julius Caesar"), England her [Cromwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Cromwell "Oliver Cromwell"), France her [Bonaparte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon "Napoleon"), and, that if we would escape the rock on which they split, we must avoid their errors."[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter2018104%E2%80%93105-99) Jackson saw Clay's protestations as an attack on his character and thus began a long rivalry between Clay and Jackson.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter2018104%E2%80%93105-99) The rivalry and the controversy over Jackson's expedition temporarily subsided after the signing of the [Adams–Onís Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams%E2%80%93On%C3%ADs_Treaty "Adams–Onís Treaty"), in which the U.S. purchased Florida and delineated its western boundary with [New Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Spain "New Spain").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010143-100)

#### 1824 presidential election

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Henry_Clay&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 1824 presidential election")]

Main article: [1824 United States presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1824_United_States_presidential_election "1824 United States presidential election")

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/ff/House_Election_of_1825.svg/500px-House_Election_of_1825.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:House_Election_of_1825.svg)

Clay helped Adams win the 1825 contingent House election after Clay failed to finish among the three electoral vote-winners. States in **orange** voted for Crawford, states in **green** for Adams, and states in **blue** for Jackson.

By 1822, several members of the Democratic-Republican Party had begun exploring presidential bids to succeed Monroe, who planned to retire after two terms like his predecessors.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010155%E2%80%93157-101) As the Federalist Party was near collapse, the 1824 presidential election would be contested only by members of the Democratic-Republican Party, including Clay. Having led the passage of the [Tariff of 1824](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tariff_of_1824 "Tariff of 1824") and the [General Survey Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Survey_Act "General Survey Act"), Clay campaigned on his American System of high tariffs and federal spending on infrastructure.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010166%E2%80%93168-102) Three members of Monroe's Cabinet, Secretary of the Treasury William Crawford, Secretary of State John Quincy Adams, and Secretary of War John C. Calhoun, appeared to be Clay's strongest competitors for the presidency.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010155%E2%80%93157-101) Though many, including Clay, did not take his candidacy seriously at first, General Andrew Jackson emerged as a presidential contender, eroding Clay's base of support in the western states.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter201899%E2%80%93101-103) In February 1824, the sparsely attended Democratic-Republican congressional caucus endorsed Crawford's candidacy, but Crawford's rivals ignored the caucus results, and various state legislatures nominated candidates for president.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter201896%E2%80%9397-104) During the campaign, Crawford suffered a major stroke, while Calhoun withdrew from the race after Jackson won the endorsement of the Pennsylvania legislature.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010162%E2%80%93164-105)

By 1824, with Crawford still in the race, Clay concluded that no candidate would win a majority of electoral votes; in that scenario, the House of Representatives would hold a [contingent election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contingent_election "Contingent election") to decide the election. Under the terms of the [Twelfth Amendment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelfth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Twelfth Amendment to the United States Constitution"), the top three electoral vote-getters would be eligible to be elected by the House. Clay was confident that he would prevail in a contingent held in the chamber he presided over, so long as he was eligible for election.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter2018110%E2%80%93112-106) Clay won Kentucky, Ohio, and Missouri, but his loss in New York and Louisiana relegated him to a fourth-place finish behind Adams, Jackson, and Crawford.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010174%E2%80%93175-107) Clay was humiliated that he finished behind the invalid Crawford and Jackson, but supporters of the three remaining presidential candidates immediately began courting his support for the contingent election.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010176-108)

For various reasons, supporters of all three candidates believed they had the best chance of winning Clay's backing, but Clay quickly settled on supporting Adams.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter2018122%E2%80%93124-109) Of the three candidates, Adams was the most sympathetic to Clay's American System, and Clay viewed both Jackson and the sickly Crawford as unsuitable for the presidency.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHargreaves198533%E2%80%9334,_36%E2%80%9338-110) On January 9, 1825, Clay privately met with Adams for three hours, after which Clay promised Adams his support; both would later claim that they did not discuss Clay's position in an Adams administration.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010179%E2%80%93180-111) With the help of Clay, Adams won the House vote on the first ballot.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010183%E2%80%93184-112) After his election, Adams offered Clay the position of secretary of state, which Clay accepted, despite fears that he would be accused of trading his support for the [Cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_the_United_States "Cabinet of the United States") post. Jackson was outraged by the election, and he and his supporters accused Clay and Adams of having reached a "[Corrupt Bargain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrupt_bargain "Corrupt bargain")".[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010184%E2%80%93185-113) Pro-Jackson forces immediately began preparing for the [1828 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1828_United_States_presidential_election "1828 United States presidential election"), with the Corrupt Bargain accusation becoming their central issue.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter2018134%E2%80%93136-114)

## Secretary of State

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Henry_Clay&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Secretary of State")]

Further information: [Presidency of John Quincy Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_John_Quincy_Adams "Presidency of John Quincy Adams")

Clay served as secretary of state from 1825 to 1829. As secretary of state, he was the top foreign policy official in the Adams administration, but he also held several domestic duties, such as oversight of the patent office.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter2018142%E2%80%93143-115) Clay came to like Adams, a former rival, and to despise Jackson. They developed a strong working relationship.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010187,_191%E2%80%93192-116) Adams and Clay were both wary of forming entangling alliances with the emerging states, and they continued to uphold the [Monroe Doctrine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monroe_Doctrine "Monroe Doctrine"), which called for European non-intervention in former colonies.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010192%E2%80%93193-117) Clay was rebuffed in his efforts to reach a commercial treaty and a settlement of the [Canada–United States border](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada%E2%80%93United_States_border "Canada–United States border") with Britain, and was also unsuccessful in his attempts to make the French pay for damages arising from attacks on American shipping during the [Napoleonic Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleonic_Wars "Napoleonic Wars").[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010192%E2%80%93193-117) He had more success in negotiating commercial treaties with Latin American republics, reaching "[most favoured nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Most_favoured_nation "Most favoured nation")" trade agreements in an attempt to ensure that no European country had a trading advantage over the United States.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGraebnerHerring2009555%E2%80%93556-118) Seeking deeper relations with Latin American countries, Clay strongly favored sending American delegates to the [Congress of Panama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congress_of_Panama "Congress of Panama"), but his efforts were defeated by opponents in the Senate.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter2018145%E2%80%93147-119)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/37/National_road_map.png/500px-National_road_map.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:National_road_map.png)

Clay supported construction of the [National Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Road "National Road"), which extended west from [Cumberland, Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cumberland,_Maryland "Cumberland, Maryland").

Adams proposed an ambitious domestic program based in large part on Clay's American System, but Clay warned the president that many of his proposals held little chance of passage in the [19th Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/19th_United_States_Congress "19th United States Congress").[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHargreaves1985165%E2%80%93166-120) Adams's opponents defeated many of his proposals, including the establishment of a naval academy and a national observatory, but Adams did preside over the construction or initiation of major infrastructure projects like the [National Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Road "National Road") and the [Chesapeake and Ohio Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chesapeake_and_Ohio_Canal "Chesapeake and Ohio Canal").[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHargreaves1985166%E2%80%93177-121) Followers of Adams began to call themselves [National Republicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Republican_Party "National Republican Party"), and Jackson's followers became known as [Democrats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)").[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler20102207-122) Both campaigns spread untrue stories about the opposing candidates.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTERemini1981134-123) Adams' followers denounced Jackson as a [demagogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demagogue "Demagogue"), and some Adams-aligned papers accused Jackson's wife [Rachel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Jackson "Rachel Jackson") of [bigamy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bigamy "Bigamy"). Though Clay was not directly involved in these attacks, his failure to denounce them earned him the lifelong enmity of Jackson.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010205%E2%80%93207-124)

Clay was one of Adams's most important political advisers, but because of his myriad responsibilities as secretary of state, he was often unable to take part in campaigning.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter2018143%E2%80%93148-125) As Adams was averse to the use of patronage for political purposes, Jackson's campaign enjoyed a marked advantage in organization, and Adams' allies such as Clay and [Daniel Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Webster "Daniel Webster") were unable to create an equally powerful organization headed by the president.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKlotter2018154%E2%80%93155-126) In the 1828 election, Jackson took 56% of the popular vote and won almost every state outside of [New England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England "New England"); Clay was especially distressed by Jackson's victory in Kentucky. The election result represented not only the victory of a man Clay viewed as unqualified and unprincipled but also a rejection of Clay's domestic policies.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Clay#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHeidlerHeidler2010212%E2%80%93213-127)
